progress.scan_network: Scanning your network for Fellow Stagg kettles…

switch_firmware.title: Switch firmware
switch_firmware.description:
The kettle runs **{running_version}** ({running_partition}). This switches it to **{target_version}** ({target_partition}), which is already stored on the kettle, and restarts it. That takes about 10 seconds.

Block the kettle's internet access first, or it may update itself again.

progress.switching: Switching the kettle to {target_version} and waiting for it to restart…

error.not_confirmed: Tick the box to confirm the switch.
error.kettle_heating: The kettle is heating. Switch firmware when it's idle.

abort.no_other_firmware: The kettle has no other valid firmware to switch to.
abort.firmware_switch_failed: The kettle didn't come back on {target_version} within a minute. Check the **Firmware version** sensor in a moment; if the switch didn't take, the kettle keeps its previous firmware.

cli_muted.title: Kettle firmware {version} stopped sharing its data
cli_muted.description:
The kettle is running firmware {version}, which no longer returns any readings over Wi-Fi, so most of its entities show *unknown*. Commands still work.

The previous firmware ({other_version}) is still on the kettle. To go back:
1. Block the kettle's internet access on your router (keep local Wi-Fi), or it will update itself again.
2. Open the Fellow Stagg integration, choose **Configure**, then **Switch firmware**.

Optionally turn on **Lock firmware** afterwards, so Home Assistant switches back if the kettle updates itself again.
